cards.title: 7.1.1 Percentage
body: Per cent (%) is a method of expressing parts of a whole, where the whole is divided into 100 parts.
Last year 1000 people were infected with malaria.
W/ro Abrhet received 10% increase in her salary.
In a community library, 24% of the books are classified as fiction.

cards.title: 7.1.2 Ratio
body: A small shop owner made a profit of 8,000.00 Nakfa one year and 24,000.00 Nakfa the next year.
**A ratio** is a comparison between quantities that are usually measured in the same units and describes the number of times that one quantity contains another quantity.
If their annual profit is 408,000.00 Nakfa, then find partner’s share.
The common ways to write the ratio m n where m and n are positive integers are: m : n, m to n or m .

cards.title: 7.1.3 Proportion
body: In each group of 7 learners there can be 2 boys.
In each group of 14 learners there can be 4 boys.
In each group of 21 learners there can be 6 boys.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Ibrahim earns a monthly salary of 2500 Nakfa. If his salary increases by $$10\%$$, find his new salary.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Calculate the increase amount**
$$\text{Increase} = 10\% \text{ of } 2500 = \frac{10}{100} \times 2500 = 250 \text{ Nakfa}$$

**Step 2: Add the increase to the original salary**
$$\text{New Salary} = 2500 + 250 = 2750 \text{ Nakfa}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
Ibrahim's new salary is **$$2750 \text{ Nakfa}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Express the ratio of 18 km to 64 km in its lowest terms.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write the ratio as a fraction**
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{18}{64}$$

**Step 2: Simplify to its lowest terms**
Divide both numerator and denominator by 2:
$$\frac{18 \div 2}{64 \div 2} = \frac{9}{32}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
In lowest terms, the ratio is **$$9 : 32$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Convert the decimal $$0.025$$ into a percentage.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Multiply the decimal by 100**
$$0.025 \times 100 = 2.5$$

**Step 2: Add the percent symbol**
$$2.5\%$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The percentage is **$$2.5\%$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Convert the percentage $$68\%$$ into its simplest fraction form.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Write as a fraction with denominator 100**
$$68\% = \frac{68}{100}$$

**Step 2: Simplify the fraction to its lowest terms**
Divide both numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, which is 4:
$$\frac{68 \div 4}{100 \div 4} = \frac{17}{25}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The simplest fraction form is **$$\frac{17}{25}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the value of $$N$$ if the ratios $$25 : N$$ and $$5 : 3$$ are proportional.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Set up the proportion equation**
$$\frac{25}{N} = \frac{5}{3}$$

**Step 2: Cross-multiply and solve for N**
$$5N = 25 \times 3$$
$$5N = 75 \implies N = 15$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The value of $$N$$ is **$$15$$**.

cards.title: 7.2.1 Commission
body: Gabriel sells instant lottery tickets, each ticket worth 5.00 Nakfa.
For every ticket he sell he gets 50 cents commission.
The payment that an agent receives for the service he or she delivers is called **commission**.
The commission is generally fixed on a percentage basis; usually known as the rate of commission, and is calculated on the total value of the sales made by the agent.

cards.title: 7.2.2 Brokerage
body: **A broker** is a person who facilitates the purchasing or the selling of properties or supplies the information needed in businesses.
**Brokerage** is the amount of money paid to the broker.
Brokerages are given usually in percentages.
Kaltum sold her house to Senay for 652,000.00 Nakfa through a broker paying 1% brokerage.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Divide 670 Nakfa in the ratio of $$3:7$$. Find the smaller portion.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Find the sum of the ratio parts**
$$\text{Total parts} = 3 + 7 = 10$$

**Step 2: Calculate the smaller portion (3 parts)**
$$\text{Smaller part} = \frac{3}{10} \times 670 = 3 \times 67 = 201 \text{ Nakfa}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The smaller portion is **$$201 \text{ Nakfa}$$**.

cards.title: Commission and brokerage — formulas
body: **Commission** is money paid to a salesperson as a percentage of the value of sales: commission = rate × sales. 5% commission on 40 000 Nakfa of sales = 0.05 × 40 000 = 2 000 Nakfa.
Some workers get a **basic salary plus commission**: total = salary + rate × sales.

**Brokerage** is the fee paid to a broker (agent) who arranges a sale or purchase between a buyer and a seller, usually a percentage of the price: brokerage = rate × price. For a 600 000 Nakfa house at 1.5%, brokerage = 9 000 Nakfa.
**Finding the rate:** rate = commission ÷ sales × 100%. **Finding the sales:** sales = commission ÷ rate.

cards.title: Worked example: salary plus commission
cards.problem: Senait earns a basic salary of 3 000 Nakfa per month plus 4% commission on sales above 20 000 Nakfa. In March she sold goods worth 65 000 Nakfa. Find her total pay.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A salesperson received 540 Nakfa commission for selling 10,800 Nakfa worth of goods. Find the rate of commission.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Apply the rate of commission formula**
$$\text{Rate of Commission} = \frac{\text{Commission}}{\text{Total Sales}} \times 100$$

**Step 2: Substitute the known values**
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{540}{10,800} \times 100 = 0.05 \times 100 = 5\%$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The rate of commission is **$$5\%$$**.

cards.title: 7.3 Profit and Loss
body: Harnet buys hens in Tserona and sells them in Dekemhare.
If cost price is greater than the selling price, then there is a loss.
Profits or losses are usually expressed in percentages relative to the cost price.
A man bought a motor cycle for 24,000 Nakfa.
A fruit vendor bought bananas for 5 Nakfa per kg.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Nasser receives a $$4\%$$ commission on all sales. If he sells 120,000 Nakfa worth of goods, how much commission will he receive?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Set up the commission calculation**
$$\text{Commission} = 4\% \text{ of } 120,000$$

**Step 2: Calculate the value**
$$\text{Commission} = \frac{4}{100} \times 120,000 = 4 \times 1200 = 4800 \text{ Nakfa}$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
He will receive a commission of **$$4800 \text{ Nakfa}$$**.

cards.title: Step by step: profit and loss
body: **Cost price (CP)** is what the seller paid; **selling price (SP)** is what the buyer pays. SP > CP → profit = SP − CP. SP < CP → loss = CP − SP.
**Percentages are on the cost price:** profit % = profit/CP × 100%; loss % = loss/CP × 100%.
Example: a trader buys a goat for 1600 Nakfa and sells it for 2000 Nakfa. Profit = 400; profit % = 400/1600 × 100% = 25%.

**Finding SP from a percentage:** SP = CP × (1 + p%) for a profit, CP × (1 − p%) for a loss. **Finding CP:** CP = SP ÷ (1 + p%). Example: sold for 1150 Nakfa at 15% profit → CP = 1150 ÷ 1.15 = 1000 Nakfa.

cards.title: Step by step: Profit and loss
body: **Step 1:** Cost price (CP) is what the trader pays; selling price (SP) is what the customer pays.
**Step 2:** If SP > CP: profit = SP − CP; if SP < CP: loss = CP − SP.
**Step 3:** Profit % = profit ÷ CP × 100 %; loss % = loss ÷ CP × 100 %.
**Step 4:** To find SP for a given profit %: SP = CP × (100 + profit %) ÷ 100.
**Step 5:** To find CP from SP: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + profit %).
**Example:** A shirt costs 250 Nakfa and the trader wants 20 % profit: SP = 250 × 120 ÷ 100 = 300 Nakfa. If it is later sold for 225 Nakfa: loss = 25 Nakfa, loss % = 25 ÷ 250 × 100 = 10 %.

cards.title: Mnemonic — "Profit and loss are percentages of the Cost"
body: always divide by CP.

cards.title: Exam tip
body: Write CP and SP clearly at the start of every problem; most errors come from dividing by SP instead of CP.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: A bicycle bought for 2500 Nakfa is sold at a loss of 12%. What is the selling price?

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A trader buys a radio for 400 Nakfa and sells it for 500 Nakfa. The profit percentage is:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Profit = selling price − cost price = 500 − 400 = 100 Nakfa.

**Step 2:** Profit % = (profit ÷ cost price) × 100 % = (100 ÷ 400) × 100 %.

**Step 3:** Answer: 25 %.

**Tip:** Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the cost price unless the question says otherwise.

cards.title: 7.4 Simple Interest
body: Azeb and Nejat tried to solve the problem as follows.
The initial amount of money invested in the bank is called the Principal (P).
The rate or percent that is stated on a specified period of time is called the simple interest rate (R).
The rate is, therefore, always represented as a decimal.
The amount of time that will be taken to pay down the debt is called time (T).

cards.title: Business mathematics
body: % = part/whole × 100
Simple interest I=Prt (t in years). Profit = SP−CP. Loss = CP−SP. Profit% = profit/CP × 100. Commission = rate × sales.

cards.title: Finding the time for simple interest
cards.problem: How long will it take 800 Nakfa to amount to 1040 Nakfa at 10% simple interest per year?

steps.text: Interest earned: I = A − P = 1040 − 800 = 240 Nakfa.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: How much simple interest does 4000 Nakfa earn in 3 years at 6% per year?
cards.why: I = P × r × t = 4000 × 0.06 × 3 = 720 Nakfa. (4720 Nakfa is the amount A = P + I, not the interest.)

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The simple interest on 2000 Nakfa at 5% per year for 3 years is:
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Formula: I = P × R × T ÷ 100.

**Step 2:** Substitute: I = 2000 × 5 × 3 ÷ 100.

**Step 3:** Answer: I = 300 Nakfa.

**Tip:** The total amount A = P + I = 2300 Nakfa – do not confuse the interest with the amount.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: At what rate of simple interest will 1500 Nakfa earn 180 Nakfa interest in 2 years?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Formula: R = (I × 100) ÷ (P × T).

**Step 2:** Substitute: R = (180 × 100) ÷ (1500 × 2) = 18 000 ÷ 3000.

**Step 3:** Answer: R = 6 % per year.

**Tip:** Rearrange I = PRT/100 before substituting to avoid arithmetic slips.

cards.title: I = PRT: "I Pay Real Taxes"
body: **I**nterest = **P**rincipal × **R**ate (as a decimal) × **T**ime (in years).
Amount A = P + I.

cards.title: Step by step: Simple interest
body: **Step 1:** Principal P is the money borrowed or saved; rate R is the percentage per year; time T is in years.
**Step 2:** Simple interest I = P × R × T ÷ 100.
**Step 3:** Amount A = P + I.
**Step 4:** Rearranged: P = 100I ÷ (RT), R = 100I ÷ (PT), T = 100I ÷ (PR).
**Step 5:** Convert months to years (÷ 12) before substituting.
**Example:** 5000 Nakfa at 8 % for 9 months: T = 9/12 = 0.75 years; I = 5000 × 8 × 0.75 ÷ 100 = 300 Nakfa; A = 5300 Nakfa.

cards.title: Mnemonic — "I = PRT over 100"
body: "Pay Rent Today".
